# FDG9055

> DO name the dependency property static field by suffixing the name of the property with “Property.”

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.3.1 Dependency Property Design.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9055
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Name the field of the dependency property '{0}' '{1}'

FDG9055 reports a static field of type DependencyProperty initialized with DependencyProperty.Register or RegisterAttached whose name is not the registered name, given as a constant string or nameof, followed by "Property"; the text's second sentence asks the same of the first argument. Registrations outside field initializers, names that are not constants, and read-only properties (whose field is taken from a DependencyPropertyKey) are not seen, so coverage is partial. Renaming a public field changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

The first parameter to the `DependencyProperty.Register` method should be the name of the wrapper property.

```csharp
public class TextButton : DependencyObject {
  public static readonly DependencyProperty TextProperty =
    DependencyProperty.Register(
      "Text",
      typeof(string),
      typeof(TextButton));
}
```
